svg.text: The same 4096 × 4096 table of 4-byte integers, walked two ways (matrix.c)
one row of the table is one run of memory;
the next row starts 16 KB later
row by row: 4 bytes to the next element,
column by column: 16 KB to the next element,
tlb2.c: ns per access vs. pages touched (one core, Xeon 2.8 GHz)
flat at about 1.3 ns: every access hits
row-major 0.010 s, column-major 0.155 s: 0.155 / 0.010 = 15.5× slower for the same additions. A column visits 4096 pages, more than the
roughly 2000 translations the TLB holds, so by the time the next column comes back to a page its row is gone, and every access misses. The data
cache misses as well (64-byte lines, one integer used per line). tlb2.c isolates the TLB alone: a miss costs about 6.2 / 1.3 ≈ 5× a hit.
